decisions.reason: Retaining the power-board I2C series resistors does not change the interboard connector architecture, signal pinout, power pinout, or connector-order policy.
The source concerns I2C series resistors, not the boost converter enable control, pull-down resistor, or powered loads.
Retaining I2C series resistors does not alter the board dimensions, orientation, mounting holes, connector placement, or enclosure-fit constraints.
The I2C resistor decision does not change the battery connector type, pin functions, mounting style, placement, or orientation.
The source does not affect battery overcharge, overdischarge, thermal, or other protection requirements.
Retaining I2C series resistors does not change battery temperature sensing through the NTC connection.
The resistor instruction does not affect the SK6812 charge-status indicator, GPIO assignment, or separate-LED policy.
The decision to retain I2C series resistors leaves the eight-layer board-stack requirement unchanged.

Even if the referenced I2C resistors correspond to listed zero-ohm components, retaining them does not remove or modify the deferred requirement to document their roles or add missing BOM part numbers.
The source specifically retains I2C series resistors and does not change the separate TVS-based ESD-protection requirement.
The I2C resistor decision does not alter the USB-C connector, its D+/D- capability, or its sourceability constraints.
